title: NY State Assembly · District 38
area: Queens: Ozone Park, Woodhaven, South Richmond Hill, and parts of Jamaica

context.text: No incumbent is on the November ballot: in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, David Orkin defeated incumbent Assembly Member Jenifer Rajkumar 58.8% to 40.9%, ending her bid for re-election. The Republican primary was canceled and Ruben Cruz II (R) advanced without appearing on the ballot.

priorities.text: "TAX THE RICH FOR AFFORDABILITY... As the richest New Yorkers and biggest corporations make more than ever, I'll fight for a state budget that asks them to pay their fair share in taxes to fund the services working people deserve: deeply affordable housing, universal childcare, guaranteed healthcare, fully funded public schools and free CUNY, world-class public transit, and more."

"PROTECT OUR IMMIGRANT NEIGHBORS. More than half of AD-38 residents are immigrants... In Albany, I'll fight to implement New York for All, ending collaboration between ICE & local law enforcement and protecting personal data from federal surveillance."

"STRENGTHEN WORKERS' RIGHTS... I'll champion the EmPIRE Worker Protection Act, which strengthens protections against wage theft, retaliation, unsafe workplaces, and union-busting. And I'll support a $30 minimum wage in New York."

positions.summary: Says he will fight to pass the New York for All Act, including provisions banning informal cooperation between local law enforcement and ICE.
positions.quote: He will fight to pass the New York for All Act in its entirety – including provisions to ban informal cooperation between local law enforcement and ICE

positions.summary: Says he will work to expand taxes on the richest New Yorkers to fund public services.
positions.quote: David will join the other Socialists in Office to expand taxes on the richest New Yorkers to fund the services working people need to thrive.

positions.summary: Says he will fight to raise the New York minimum wage to $30 by 2030.
positions.quote: raise the minimum wage to $30 by 2030

positions.summary: Says he will join the fight for the New York Health Act to create universal healthcare statewide.
positions.quote: He'll join the fight for the New York Health Act to create universal healthcare for all New Yorkers statewide

positions.summary: Says he will champion the Universal Child Care Act to provide free, high-quality care for all New Yorkers.
positions.quote: David will champion the Universal Child Care Act to provide free, high-quality care for all New Yorkers

positions.summary: Says he will restore the full Climate Leadership and Community Protection Act, implement the Build Public Renewables Act and pass the NY HEAT Act to end subsidies for fossil fuel expansion.
positions.quote: restoring the full CLCPA and implementing the Build Public Renewables Act to build more publicly owned, nonprofit, renewable energy sources using union labor

positions.summary: Says he will strengthen Good Cause Eviction protections statewide and pass the Right to Counsel Act for tenants.
positions.quote: David will strengthen Good Cause Eviction protections statewide.

candidates.name: Ruben Cruz II

priorities.text: On transit: "I will audit the MTA to bridge the... transit desert between Woodside and Woodhaven with reliable, eco-friendly bus service. We must address the alarming pollution levels in our subways to protect our health."

On homeowner protections: "I am fighting for economic justice for homeowners: I will legislate to ban property liens placed without owner knowledge and eliminate the hidden bank and utility fees that drain blue-collar paychecks."

On seniors and pets: "I am committed to preserving the rights of residents over 62 to live with their pets without housing discrimination and advocating for pet-friendly shelters so no neighbor is forced into homelessness to stay with a loved one."

candidates.researchNotes: His campaign site (rubencruz.nyc) was reviewed; its rent-stabilization comment concerns commercial tenants and its education page does not address funding for charters or vouchers, so no statements or stances on the guide's issues are recorded.

sources.title: David Orkin - Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey
Ruben Cruz II - Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey

researchNotes: Neither candidate has held elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record for either. Orkin's positions are documented in depth from his campaign's detailed platform statements and Ballotpedia survey. Cruz completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey with extensive priorities in his own words, but did not take clear stances on this guide's fixed issue list, so no Position entries are included for him; his research depth is marked 'basic' accordingly. Biographies draw on candidates' own materials plus Ballotpedia and two news reports on Orkin; no news profile of Cruz II was found.
